info.title: BABY Observability API
info.description: Operational observability and audit visibility API for the BABY platform. Read-only except for task control (submit, cancel, admin approval decisions), which only writes durable task state; tasks execute in isolated worker processes. All endpoints enforce authentication and engagement scoping.

get.description: Read-only health representation distinguishing healthy, degraded, and unavailable states.

Readiness check: confirms Baby can safely accept and process work.

Returns 200 OK when ready, 503 Service Unavailable when not ready.
Available under both /ready and /readiness.

Readiness check: confirms Baby can safely accept and process work.

Returns 200 OK when ready, 503 Service Unavailable when not ready.
Available under both /ready and /readiness.

Expose snapshot of bounded operational metrics.

Counters and latencies describe events seen by this API process. Tasks run in worker
processes, so ``gauges.tasks_by_status`` is read from the durable store instead of
in-process counters (which would show every task as still pending).

Expose safe read-only operational information about tasks.

Scope is determined by caller's server-side authorized engagements.
The engagement_id query parameter selects within that set; it cannot
expand the caller's authorization beyond what was configured server-side.

Retrieve detailed read-only state for a specific task.

IDOR protection: the task's stored user_id is checked against the caller's
server-side authorized engagements. Knowing a task UUID is not sufficient
to access it across engagement boundaries.

post.description:
Durably enqueue a task for execution by a worker process.

The task's engagement is resolved server-side from the caller's authorized scope;
the request can only *select* one of the caller's engagements, never expand it.
Nothing is executed by the API: a worker claims the task asynchronously.

With an ``Idempotency-Key`` the submission happens at most once per
(principal, engagement, key), across retries, concurrent requests and restarts.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Optional client-chosen key (1-255 visible ASCII characters, e.g. a UUID). Scoped to the authenticated principal and the resolved engagement. Repeating it with an identical request returns the original task (replayed=true) instead of creating a duplicate; repeating it with a different request returns 409. Keys are kept as long as the task record exists.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Optional client-chosen key (1-255 visible ASCII characters, e.g. a UUID). Scoped to the authenticated principal and the resolved engagement. Repeating it with an identical request returns the original task (replayed=true) instead of creating a duplicate; repeating it with a different request returns 409. Keys are kept as long as the task record exists.

503.description: The task was persisted but its TASK_CREATED audit event could not be written. Retrying with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same task and records the event once.

post.description: Cancel a task in the caller's engagement (immediately, or at the worker's next lease renewal).

Approve or deny one pending approval request. Admin role required.

The decision is bound to the task, its engagement and the exact operation digest
recorded in the request; approving lets a worker execute that one operation once.
A request older than ``approval_ttl_seconds`` can no longer be decided: the task is
failed closed and 409 is returned.

get.description: Expose safe operational visibility into background/pool workers.
Retrieve operational state for a specific worker.

Expose safe read-only visibility into registered agents.

Includes agents registered in this process and, because tasks run in worker processes,
the agents hosted by live durable workers.
Retrieve safe operational visibility into a specific agent.

Retrieve filtered, engagement-scoped audit records with sensitive details redacted.

Authorization: caller.restrict_to_engagement() enforces that the requested scope
is within the caller's server-side-configured allowed_engagements set.
The X-Engagement-ID header (captured at auth time) is not used here; callers
must pass engagement_id as a query parameter to scope their query explicitly.

TaskStatus.title: TaskStatus
TaskStatus.description:
Execution status of a task.

State machine:
    PENDING → IN_PROGRESS | CANCELLED
    IN_PROGRESS → AWAITING_APPROVAL | COMPLETED | FAILED | CANCELLED
    AWAITING_APPROVAL → IN_PROGRESS | FAILED | CANCELLED
    COMPLETED → (terminal — no further transitions)
    FAILED → (terminal — no further transitions)
    CANCELLED → (terminal — no further transitions)

TaskSubmission.title: TaskSubmission
TaskSubmission.description: Request body for durable task submission.

TaskView.title: TaskView
TaskView.description: Operational record for one task. ``status`` follows the authoritative state machine.

WorkerStatus.title: WorkerStatus
WorkerStatus.description:
Operational status of a worker.

Durable worker processes move through:
    STARTING → IDLE ⇄ BUSY → STOPPING → STOPPED
and may be marked by recovery as:
    STALE  — heartbeat older than ``worker_stale_timeout_seconds``
    ERROR  — process exited abnormally or failed fatally
IDLE/BUSY/STARTING/STOPPING with a fresh heartbeat count as alive.

WorkerView.title: WorkerView
WorkerView.description: Worker operational status. Host/process metadata is withheld from non-admin callers.
